Here's the V8-Powered 2028 BMW Alpina 7 Series Hitting Over 300 KPH at Nardo
9 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW could have easily made the Alpina-branded 7 Series a performance statement. Instead of creating an M7 under a different name, the German automaker decided that its upcoming flagship sedan model should be able to hit 300 kilometers per hour (186 miles per hour) in superlative comfort.
Pictured under camouflage, the V8-powered newcomer has already exceeded 300 clicks at Nardo. Due to hit dealers in 2027, the BMW Alpina 7 Series is all about comfort, precision, stability, and the ability to cover long distances without exhausting the person behind the wheel or those seated in the back. Put another way, BMW has created a very different sedan from the long-rumored M7.
Equipped with 20-spoke alloys that are unmistakably Alpina in their design, the camouflaged prototype also features production-intent lights and bumpers. The front and rear bumpers, along with the quad oval exhaust finishers, also differentiate this model from its BMW-only equivalent.
BMW says the Alpina-exclusive alloys were developed alongside specific tires, with said tires incorporating a foam layer. That layer is key to high speeds in such a heavy vehicle, with the BMW Alpina 7 Series expected to weigh over two metric tons when equipped with the S68 twin-turbo V8.
What I find even more interesting about said layer is that BMW puts a bigger emphasis on driving comfort and precision rather than outright speed. While anyone can advertise a ridiculously high top speed, few automakers understand that comfort matters a lot more in the long run. Similarly, precision sits really high on the list of priorities of anyone who loves driving.
Photo: BMW BMW hasn't disclosed the maximum output figures of the S68 under its hood, but due to its Alpina branding, look forward to revised accelerator pedal mapping and engine management, all in the name of smoothness and responsiveness over aggressive power and torque delivery. Of course, BMW has recalibrated the ZF-supplied automatic transmission for this application as well.
A comfortable yet dynamic chassis setup also needs highlighting, while aerodynamic tweaks promise stability at Autobahn speeds. Based on the details shared by the Bavarian automaker until now, the BMW Alpina 7 Series isn't chasing one particularly impressive specification. Rather, the automaker wants the engine, tranny, and chassis to work together seamlessly.
Just like the regular 7 Series and a few other BMW models, the BMW Alpina sedan brings navigation-guided driver assistance functions. To be introduced next year, the system can assist with urban lane changes, turns, roundabouts, and in right-of-way situations. BMW further plans to extend its Motorway Assistant concept across country roads and into the urban jungle.
Being a Level 2 system, the driver must remain attentive, ready to take control whenever the situation calls for human intervention. BMW Symbiotic Drive blurs the line between semi-autonomous driving and human intervention, letting the driver accelerate, steer, and brake while the assistance system operates.
Internally referred to as G72, the BMW Alpina 7 Series is expected to enter production in July 2027 for the 2028 model year. Three specifications are understood to launch for 2028, namely the six-pot 740 xDrive, eight-cylinder 760 xDrive, and the zero-emission i7 70 xDrive.
